sections.overview: Elops machnata is a tropical Indo-West Pacific ladyfish, related to West African E. lacerta and E. senegalensis.
sections.identification: It has an elongated body, a gular plate and an upper jaw extending behind the eye.
sections.habitat: It frequents coastal marine waters and enters lagoons and estuaries.
sections.diet: Young and adults feed on small fish and crustaceans.
sections.behavior: Its transparent larvae migrate from offshore spawning areas towards inshore and brackish waters.
sections.reproduction: Spawning probably occurs at sea, although the available sources give no precise season.
sections.ecology: It shares a coastal-pelagic lifestyle with E. lacerta and E. senegalensis but occupies a different ocean region.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a global IUCN category of Least Concern, assessed in 2016.
